_note: Program facts below were checked against the official pages listed in each entry on the verified_on date. Numeric fields marked as assumptions (assumed_award_usd, loan sizing) are RailPlanner screening assumptions, not program limits. Re-verify against the current NOFO before relying on any of this.

programs.name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (National)
programs.notes: Primary federal capital program for intercity passenger rail outside the Northeast Corridor main line.

guide.applicants: States (including DC), groups of States, interstate compacts, public agencies or authorities established by States, political subdivisions, Amtrak, federally recognized Tribes, or combinations of these.
guide.stage: Capital projects, or planning, environmental review and final design of an eligible project. Competitive applications generally show a service development plan and progress through environmental review.
guide.match: Federal share may not exceed 80% of project cost (49 U.S.C. 24911); at least 20% non-federal.
guide.limits: No fixed award cap is published. RailPlanner assumes a largest single award of $3.0B for screening; this is an assumption, not a program limit.
guide.status: FY2024–2026 round closed; project selections announced August 14, 2026. No open round listed as of the verification date.
guide.next_step: Advance the corridor through Corridor ID (service development plan, then preliminary engineering and environmental review) so it is ready for the next FSP-National notice.
guide.fit_rule: 0.90 if the median cost is $1B or more (the program's core use), otherwise 0.65. Eligible for either project type.
guide.source_label: FRA, National Railroad Partnership Program page

programs.name: Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (Northeast Corridor)
programs.notes: Limited to projects on the Northeast Corridor (Washington–Boston main line).

guide.applicants: Same eligible recipients as FSP-National; projects must be located on the Northeast Corridor.
guide.stage: Projects listed in, or consistent with, FRA's Northeast Corridor Project Inventory.
guide.match: Federal share may not exceed 80% of project cost (49 U.S.C. 24911).
guide.limits: Only the Northeast Corridor portion of a route can qualify. RailPlanner assumes a largest single award of $4.0B for screening.
guide.status: FY2025–2026 round (applications due May 5, 2026) closed; selections announced. No open round listed as of the verification date.
guide.next_step: Coordinate with Amtrak and the NEC Commission to have any Northeast Corridor elements (for example, New York approaches) included in the NEC Project Inventory.
guide.fit_rule: 0.60 if the route uses the New York–Philadelphia main line; 0.35 if it only reaches New York City; otherwise not a fit.
guide.source_label: FRA, National Railroad Partnership Program page (Partnership-NEC section)
unverified_fields: share of route cost attributable to the NEC (RailPlanner assumption)

programs.name: Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI)
programs.notes: Safety, efficiency and reliability improvements for intercity passenger and freight rail, including grade crossings and capacity on existing lines.

guide.applicants: States, groups of States, interstate compacts, public agencies, political subdivisions, Amtrak and other rail carriers providing intercity passenger service, Class II and III railroads, and others listed in 49 U.S.C. 22907.
guide.stage: Discrete capital packages (grade crossings, sidings, signals, track and bridge work) and related planning, environmental and design work.
guide.match: Federal share may not exceed 80% of project cost (49 U.S.C. 22907).
guide.limits: No fixed award cap is published. RailPlanner assumes a largest single award of $250M, so CRISI suits packages, not a whole corridor.
guide.status: FY2025–2026 round closed; selections announced October 19, 2026. No open round listed as of the verification date.
guide.next_step: Identify discrete safety and capacity packages on the existing corridor (grade crossings, sidings) with the host railroad, ready for the next CRISI notice.
guide.fit_rule: 0.80 for routes mostly on existing rail (where CRISI-type work concentrates), 0.55 for new alignments.

programs.name: BUILD (formerly RAISE) Grants
programs.notes: Competitive surface transportation grants with a maximum award of $25M; suited to a station or grade separation, not a corridor.

guide.applicants: States and DC, territories, local governments, public agencies or authorities established by States, special-purpose districts with a transportation function, Tribes, transit agencies, and multi-State or multi-jurisdictional groups of eligible entities.
guide.stage: Capital projects (minimum award $5M urban, $1M rural) or planning, preparation and design (no minimum).
guide.match: Federal share may not exceed 80% for urban projects; it may exceed 80% for rural projects and those in Areas of Persistent Poverty or Historically Disadvantaged Communities.
guide.status: FY2026 round closed (applications were due February 24, 2026). A FY2027 notice had not been found as of the verification date.
guide.next_step: Package a station, grade separation or design phase as a stand-alone application for the next BUILD round.
guide.fit_rule: 0.45 for any route: useful for components, not the core build.
guide.source_label: USDOT, FY2026 BUILD Frequently Asked Questions

programs.name: Railroad Rehabilitation and Improvement Financing (RRIF)
programs.notes: Direct loans and loan guarantees that must be repaid.

guide.applicants: Public and private sponsors of railroad projects, including state and local governments, government-sponsored authorities and railroads.
guide.stage: Projects with a defined scope, cost estimate and a dedicated repayment source; the Bureau's credit review takes place after initial consultation.
guide.match: Not a grant: a loan that must be repaid. Can finance up to 100% of eligible project costs.
guide.limits: Repayment up to 35 years (in some cases 75), at the government's cost of borrowing. RailPlanner sizes the loan at 20% of the median cost to illustrate financing a non-federal share; this is an assumption.
guide.status: Applications are handled through the Build America Bureau rather than a fixed funding round. The application timetable was not confirmed on the verification date.
guide.next_step: Identify a repayment source (state appropriations, farebox or value capture) and request an initial consultation with the Build America Bureau.
guide.fit_rule: 0.70 for routes mostly on existing rail, 0.60 for new alignments; fit depends on having a repayment source, which is not modeled.
guide.source_label: USDOT Build America Bureau, RRIF page
unverified_fields: use alongside federal grants for the non-federal share

programs.name: Corridor Identification and Development Program (Corridor ID)
programs.notes: Planning and development pipeline for intercity passenger rail corridors.

guide.applicants: Amtrak, States, groups of States, entities implementing interstate compacts, regional passenger rail authorities, regional planning organizations, political subdivisions and federally recognized Tribes.
guide.stage: Entry point for a new or improved corridor, before a service development plan.
guide.match: Initial award of $500,000 per selected corridor for Step 1 scoping. Later steps (service development plan, then preliminary engineering and environmental review) have their own funding terms set in the program notice.
guide.status: Corridors were selected from the FY2022 solicitation (announced December 8, 2023). No new solicitation was listed as of the verification date.
guide.next_step: Check whether an overlapping corridor is already in the program and coordinate with its sponsor; otherwise prepare a corridor proposal for the next solicitation.
guide.fit_rule: 0.95 for any intercity corridor: it is the planning gateway FRA uses to build its capital project pipeline.
